acceptanceClaims: the first successor fully materialized peer B, the maintained Windows Guest consumed the one-shot peer-B service and completed, and the successor was SIGKILLed before peer-b-present/currentPeerAddress/peer identity were durably published
the durable ledger digest remained unchanged across completed physical consequence and successor death while persistent Host topology already showed complete peer B

a second lineage-linked successor acquired recovery authority against that same unpublished durable generation and independently recovered persistent topology, the completed Guest result from the closed run disk, and read-only packet-sensor evidence showing both peer-A and peer-B flows
the corrected sensor observation left the capture process alive before and after the read and attempted no capture mutation

the second successor classified completed-but-unpublished, did not restart the transient peer-B service, did not replay or mutate the Range world, and repaired only durable peer-b-present publication with peerPid=0/peerStartTime=null
final reconciliation preserved current plus archived successor claims, closed the still-live capture and remaining Range substrate, and left zero residuals

methodologyCandidate.reason: the candidate reused a helper that terminated tcpdump before reading pcap, so it was not accepted as evidence-preserving no-world-replay methodology

limitations: the experiment proves recovery only for the exact isolated S6 peer-replacement consequence with persistent topology plus matching Guest and sensor evidence
Guest and packet-sensor evidence are treated as independent evidence planes, not infallible world truth
effects whose delivered and undelivered histories converge to an observationally identical world remain untested
generic exactly-once delivery, arbitrary non-idempotent effects, shared-resource concurrency and causal-DAG requirements remain unproved
the accepted Range remains structurally unrouted and does not authorize external or uncontrolled targets
